session.question: In hepatocellular carcinoma, what was found about macrophage migration inhibitory factor, and how did its knockdown affect tumor cell behavior and related protein expression?
session.answer:
Macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) was significantly upregulated in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) tissues and cell lines relative to adjacent normal liver tissue or a normal liver cell line. In HCC specimens, MIF expression positively correlated with cyclin D1 expression and with tumor size. (huang2014smallinterferingrna chunk 1)

siRNA-mediated knockdown of MIF in PLC and HepG2 cells inhibited cell proliferation, promoted apoptosis, and reduced xenograft tumor growth. One report noted that MIF knockdown did not alter the cell cycle. (huang2014smallinterferingrna chunk 1)

At the protein level, MIF knockdown downregulated cyclin D1, p-Akt, and p-ERK, consistent with suppression of growth and survival signaling. It also upregulated apoptosis-associated proteins Bcl-2, p-caspase-3, BIM, and Bax. (huang2014smallinterferingrna chunk 1)

pqac-b651852c: The study found that macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) was significantly upregulated in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) tissues and cell lines compared with adjacent normal liver tissue or a normal liver cell line. In HCC specimens, MIF expression positively correlated with cyclin D1 expression and with tumor size. When MIF was knocked down by siRNA, proliferation of PLC and HepG2 cells was inhibited, apoptosis was promoted, and tumor growth was reduced in a xenograft model. MIF knockdown also changed protein expression: cyclin D1, p-Akt, and p-ERK were downregulated, while Bcl-2, p-caspase-3, BIM, and Bax were upregulated.
From Xiao-hui Huang, Wei-hua Jian, Zhao-feng Wu, Jie Zhao, Hua Wang, Wen Li, and Jin-tang Xia. Small interfering rna (sirna)-mediated knockdown of macrophage migration inhibitory factor (mif) suppressed cyclin d1 expression and hepatocellular carcinoma cell proliferation. Oncotarget, 2014. URL: https://doi.org/10.18632/oncotarget.2141, doi:10.18632/oncotarget.2141.

pqac-631d9740: This study examined macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). MIF and cyclin D1 were significantly upregulated in HCC tissues and cell lines versus normal controls, and their expression positively correlated with each other and with tumor size. siRNA-mediated MIF knockdown in PLC and HepG2 cells inhibited proliferation, promoted apoptosis, and reduced xenograft tumor growth. It did not affect the cell cycle. After MIF knockdown, apoptosis-related proteins Bcl-2, p-caspase-3, BIM, and Bax were increased, while growth-related proteins cyclin D1, p-Akt, and p-ERK were decreased, suggesting MIF as a therapeutic target.
From Xiao-hui Huang, Wei-hua Jian, Zhao-feng Wu, Jie Zhao, Hua Wang, Wen Li, and Jin-tang Xia. Small interfering rna (sirna)-mediated knockdown of macrophage migration inhibitory factor (mif) suppressed cyclin d1 expression and hepatocellular carcinoma cell proliferation. Oncotarget, 2014. URL: https://doi.org/10.18632/oncotarget.2141, doi:10.18632/oncotarget.2141.

pqac-f91b76c2: The excerpt is about TIPE2 in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), not macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF). It reports that forced TIPE2 expression in HCC cell lines inhibits tumor cell growth, migration, and invasion in vitro and suppresses growth and metastasis in vivo. In 112 patient samples, reduced TIPE2 expression in primary HCC was associated with metastasis. Mechanistically, TIPE2 inhibits migration and invasion by targeting Rac1, which reduces F-actin polymerization and lowers expression of MMP9 and uPA. The excerpt does not mention MIF knockdown specifically, but it does describe tumor cell behavior and protein expression changes in HCC.
From Xuelei Cao, Li Zhang, Yongyu Shi, Yue Sun, Shen Dai, Chun Guo, Faliang Zhu, Qun wang, Jianing Wang, Xiaoyan Wang, Youhai H Chen, and Lining Zhang. Human tumor necrosis factor (tnf)-alpha-induced protein 8-like 2 suppresses hepatocellular carcinoma metastasis through inhibiting rac1. Molecular Cancer, 2013. URL: https://doi.org/10.1186/1476-4598-12-149, doi:10.1186/1476-4598-12-149.

pqac-a210478d: This paper studies hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cell behavior in vasculogenic mimicry (VM) and the role of RhoA/ROCK signaling, not macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF). It reports that HCC cells with higher active RhoA/ROCK expression formed more VM channels, while the ROCK inhibitor Y27632 dose-dependently blocked tubular network formation, migration, and invasion. ROCK inhibition also reduced expression of VM-related and EMT-associated proteins/markers such as VE-cadherin, EphA2, PI3K, MMP14, MMP2, MMP9, LAMC2, E-cadherin, and Vimentin. The excerpt does not mention MIF knockdown or MIF-specific protein expression changes.
From Ji-Gang Zhang, Xiao-Yu Li, Yu-Zhu Wang, Qi-Di Zhang, Sheng-Ying Gu, Xin Wu, Guan-Hua Zhu, Qin Li, and Gao-Lin Liu. Rock is involved in vasculogenic mimicry formation in hepatocellular carcinoma cell line. PLoS ONE, 2014. URL: https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0107661, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0107661.

pqac-48186dc5: The excerpt is about TIPE2, not macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF). It reports that TIPE2 is downregulated in human hepatocellular carcinoma and functions as an endogenous inhibitor of Rac1, suppressing tumor growth, migration, invasion, and metastasis. Forced expression of TIPE2 in HCC cell lines inhibited migration and invasion in vitro and reduced growth/metastasis in vivo. Mechanistically, TIPE2 reduced Rac1 activity, F-actin polymerization, and the expression of MMP9 and uPA, and loss/reduced TIPE2 in patient tumors was associated with metastasis.
From Xuelei Cao, Li Zhang, Yongyu Shi, Yue Sun, Shen Dai, Chun Guo, Faliang Zhu, Qun wang, Jianing Wang, Xiaoyan Wang, Youhai H Chen, and Lining Zhang. session.formatted_answer:
Question: In hepatocellular carcinoma, what was found about macrophage migration inhibitory factor, and how did its knockdown affect tumor cell behavior and related protein expression?

Macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) was significantly upregulated in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) tissues and cell lines relative to adjacent normal liver tissue or a normal liver cell line. In HCC specimens, MIF expression positively correlated with cyclin D1 expression and with tumor size. (huang2014smallinterferingrna chunk 1)

siRNA-mediated knockdown of MIF in PLC and HepG2 cells inhibited cell proliferation, promoted apoptosis, and reduced xenograft tumor growth. One report noted that MIF knockdown did not alter the cell cycle. (huang2014smallinterferingrna chunk 1)

At the protein level, MIF knockdown downregulated cyclin D1, p-Akt, and p-ERK, consistent with suppression of growth and survival signaling. It also upregulated apoptosis-associated proteins Bcl-2, p-caspase-3, BIM, and Bax. (huang2014smallinterferingrna chunk 1)
